<title
    level="1"
    right="Feat 2"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[Cooperative Crafting](/Feats.aspx?ID=4166) <actions string="" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Uncommon" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=159" />
<trait label="General" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=78" />
<trait label="Skill" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=144" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Highhelm](/Sources.aspx?ID=204) pg. 72

**Prerequisites**
Expert in [Crafting](/Skills.aspx?ID=4)

</column>

---

You've learned to make the most of working with others on your crafting projects, a must when working with the various guilds of Highhelm. If an ally is attempting to [Aid](/Actions.aspx?ID=75) you with your Crafting, you ignore the –1 circumstance penalty if they roll a critical failure. If an ally also has the Cooperative Crafting feat, you can choose to pool your resources and work on the same item together; you can only work with 1 ally in this way. Both of you attempt a Crafting check on the same item; if you both succeed, reduce the minimum time to craft the item by 1 day. When determining the level of item you and your ally can craft, you use the higher of your level or your ally's level plus 1. If you attempt to [Craft](/Actions.aspx?ID=43) an item that's a higher level than either of you and one of you fails, both checks become critical failures instead.
name: Cooperative Crafting
